messages:
Maria: Heads up: this morning at ~07:12 UTC we saw a spike in DEK-decrypt errors for the encryption service. logs show 503s from aws-kms for ~90s. :rotating_light:
Alex: saw the alert, ETA? any customer impact?
Maria: small - <0.5% of requests errored and retried successfully. we hit our fallback path but noticed some decrypts were returning 'InvalidCiphertext' intermittently. no repeated user-visible failures.
Sanjay: throwing the relevant snippet here: ```2026-02-01T07:12:23Z ERROR decrypt failed kms=aws region=us-east-1 code=ThrottlingException retry=1 svc=encryption`InvalidCiphertext` after 3 attempts```
Eve: InvalidCiphertext during normal decrypts usually means the DEK used to encrypt doesn't match the KMS key version used to decrypt (key id mismatch) or the ciphertext got corrupted. Could this be a race with the key rotation we ran yesterday?
Alex: we rotated the wrapping key at 2026-01-31T23:45 UTC, yes. ops-bot shows the rotation completed but the KMS admin policy change rolled out a few minutes later.
ops-bot: notice: key-rotation (key-arn: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd) completed; IAM policy updated by Kei.
Kei: I pushed an RBAC tighten for the encryption service role to remove kms:Decrypt for older aliases as part of cleanup. I thought the alias mapping would be seamless, but maybe there was a propagation gap.
Maria: that aligns — timeline: rotation -> policy update -> ~+3m we see decrypts start failing and then slow 503s. The service's caching layer had several stale DEKs pinned (in-memory) and those couldn't be re-wrapped quickly due to KMS throttling.
Sanjay: mitigation we used: 1) temporarily re-enabled broader decrypt permissions for the service role, 2) flushed the local DEK cache (rolling restart of a subset), 3) applied increased KMS retry jitter and backoff. That stopped new failures within ~4 minutes.
Eve: good. Need to check audit logs: does CloudTrail show the failed decrypt calls and policy denies? we should confirm if the failures were 'ThrottlingException' or explicit 'AccessDenied' in each case.
Maria: CloudTrail shows mix: many ThrottlingExceptions at the start, then AccessDenied for calls where alias->key binding didn't match because of the tightened policy. So both factors combined.
Alex: action items: short-term doc for runbook tweaks, longer-term: ensure rotation + RBAC changes are coordinated (lock-step), add a pre-rotation probe that verifies alias resolution and a canary decrypt flow across zones, and add DEK staleness detection.
Kei: agreed. I'll roll back the RBAC tighten in prod and prepare a staged policy rollout for next rotation.
Sanjay: also proposing a new metric: ratio of DEK cache hit decrypt failures per minute; alert if >0 for 1m. plus a circuit-breaker that rejects requests when KMS error rate > threshold and routes to degraded path (pre-warmed local rewrap).
Eve: add audit: include key-version metadata in our access logs for every encrypt/decrypt so post-rotation troubleshooting is easier.
Maria: follow-up: I'll open an incident follow-up doc and schedule a postmortem in eng-security tomorrow. For now: rollback RBAC, increase retry window to 30s with capped jitter, and flush cache in a controlled rolling fashion.
Alex: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deployment note: rolled policy rollback queued for 07:35 UTC; watch for CloudTrail logs and service metrics.
Kei: will add a gating check to the rotation job: verify alias->keyid mapping from each region and run a canary decrypt before any RBAC tighten.
Maria: tagging this as near-miss. no P0 but we should treat as high-severity process gap.
Sanjay: I'll draft the runbook changes and a short AM/PM checklist for rotations.
Eve: assigning audit review to me. will validate CloudTrail integrity and export events to secure S3 bucket for retention.
Maria: end of thread — will paste the incident doc link when ready.
